lines.text: In 1939, at the New York World's Fair, Bell Labs showed off a machine that could talk. It was called the Voder.
Few believed a machine would ever sound human.
In 1961, an IBM computer at Bell Labs sang a song. Daisy Bell.
Fifty years later, phones started talking back.
Then neural networks learned to breathe, pause and laugh.
The voice you're hearing right now took seconds to make. One line of text. Any language. Any tone.
Nearly a century later, the narrator is just another setting in your edit. Follow for more vibe editing.
